newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Truck offers soften on supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Truck offers soften on supply.

text.p: Some offers for soybean meal by truck in U.S. cash markets were lower Tuesday, under pressure from growing supplies, brokers said.
Crushers were said to be running at a brisk pace while demand for soymeal from domestic end-users and exporters was slowing in front of the Christmas holiday, dealers said.

"Crushers will run through the holiday, but at the same time you have half the time to sell the stuff," one Minnesota-based broker said, noting that some crushing plants will be operating on Christmas and New Years Day.
"Out of ten days you would normally have to sell, you only have eight days because of the holidays," the broker said.
Bitterly cold temperatures throughout the Midwest mean that crushers would continue to run at a high pace because it is too hard to restart plants in cold weather, one dealer said.
There were also rumors circulating in the cash and futures markets that China has made a number of price inquiries on soymeal from South America, traders said.
However, no business could be confirmed.
